audit_findings.title: Parent earnings are mixed with consolidated add-backs and assets
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated D&A, capex, working-capital adjustments and cash enter parent-level OE and the equity bridge without consistently removing MGM China noncontrolling interests.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we operate 16 domestic casino properties and, through our approximate 56% controlling interest in MGM China Holdings Limited (together with its subsidiaries, “MGM China”), which owns MGM Grand Paradise, S.A. (“MGM Grand Paradise”), operate two casino properties in Macau.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter inconsistency, not merely a possible risk. MGM owns approximately 56% of MGM China, while the valuation begins with earnings attributable to MGM shareholders but uses consolidated adjustments and cash. The filing reports $315.010 million of 2025 net income attributable to noncontrolling interests and $514 million of MGM China cash at June 30, 2026, showing that third-party economics are substantial. The exact valuation overstatement cannot be computed from the supplied components, but it is reasonably capable of changing the $41.44 base conclusion, which is only $0.22 above the $41.22 market price.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every OE year using parent-attributable D&A, capex, working capital and other adjustments; separately identify MGM China cash, debt and required regulatory or operating cash; then rerun all scenarios and the bridge using only MGM-parent economics.

audit_findings.title: The perpetual terminal value crosses MGM China’s 2032 concession cliff
audit_findings.mechanism: The terminal value perpetuates MGM China OE beyond December 31, 2032 without an explicit concession-renewal probability, revised economics or renewal investment.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, the concession contract expires on December 31, 2032.
audit_findings.explanation: The concession expiration is filed, while MGM China is material: it produced $1.203 billion of 2025 Segment Adjusted EBITDAR and $4.462 billion of revenue. Terminal value represents 47.7% to 50.9% of operating value across the scenarios, so an unadjusted perpetuity extends a material contributor beyond a legally finite right. Renewal may occur, so loss after 2032 is not demonstrated, but the omitted cliff is clearly capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Isolate parent-attributable MGM China OE, value it through 2032 as finite-lived, and rerun using explicit post-2032 renewal probabilities, concession economics, fees and required investments; disclose the zero-renewal case.

audit_findings.title: Osaka’s $2.3 billion remaining funding commitment is outside reported OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.1 billion remaining at June 30, 2026, about $8.15 per diluted share and 19.7% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Committed contributions are investing cash flows outside reported OE and therefore require either an equity-bridge deduction or an explicitly modeled Osaka project value net of all remaining funding.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to fund the estimated remaining amount of approximately JPY356.9 billion (approximately $2.3 billion as of December 31, 2025 ) on a quarterly basis through 2028, of which a portion we expect to fund in 2026 with the proceeds from the senior secured yen credit facility.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing confirms $2.1 billion remains committed through 2028, plus an uncapped completion-funding guarantee. The commitment equals roughly $8.15 per valuation share versus base value of $41.44 and is therefore plainly conclusion-changing if the credited Osaka value does not fully compensate for it. This is a demonstrated omission from recurring OE, although the net project value and guarantee exposure remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $2.1 billion remaining commitment, the subsequent $18 million July contribution, yen financing, hedges, interest, ownership dilution and the uncapped guarantee; then rerun the bridge with remaining funding deducted exactly once and any independently supported Osaka value credited exactly once.

audit_findings.title: The $877 million stakes bridge may double count affiliate value
audit_findings.mechanism: Affiliate income, losses or distributions may remain in operating OE while the same affiliates are separately added through the $877 million stakes bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company classifies operating income and losses as well as gains and impairments related to its investments in unconsolidated affiliates as a component of operating income or loss and classifies non-operating income or losses related to its investments in unconsolidated affiliates as a component of non-operating income or loss, as the Company’s investments in such unconsolidated affiliates are an extension of the Company’s core business operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings establish that unconsolidated-affiliate results enter operating income and show $69.982 million of 2025 operating income from affiliates, including $59.634 million from BetMGM. They do not establish which assets compose stakes_net or which affiliate economics were removed from OE. Double counting is therefore unresolved rather than demonstrated. The possible exposure is potentially important because the entire $877 million bridge equals about $3.41 per share, but the overlapping amount cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Produce an asset-by-asset schedule for stakes_net, map each asset to OE adjustments, distributions, contributions and carrying or market value, and rerun after eliminating any duplicated earnings or stake value.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter may ignore the MGM Northfield Park sale
audit_findings.magnitude: $541 million net proceeds, $53 million annual rent reduction, and $44.464 million of H1 2026 pre-sale Segment Adjusted EBITDAR
audit_findings.mechanism: FY2025 OE includes Northfield operations, while the June 2026 cash bridge follows the April 2026 sale and includes proceeds; removing the business lowers OE, while the rent reduction and retained proceeds increase value.
audit_findings.evidence: In October 2025, we entered into an agreement to sell the operations of MGM Northfield Park for $ 546 million in cash, subject to customary purchase price adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q confirms that the sale closed in April 2026, so the null perimeter is a demonstrated mismatch. The $541 million net proceeds entered 2026 investing cash flow, while the FY2025 anchor still contains Northfield operations. The direction is mixed because normalized OE must lose Northfield earnings but gain the $53 million annual rent reduction, and proceeds must be recognized only once. With base value only $0.22 above market price, the unresolved net adjustment is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Build a Northfield carve-out from FY2025 OE, incorporate the post-sale rent reduction and taxes, trace the $541 million proceeds into June 2026 cash, remove restricted or operating cash, and rerun the valuation on the June 2026 perimeter without counting proceeds twice.

audit_findings.title: Large landlord-debt guarantees are not covered by MGM interest expense
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.01 billion filed principal face amount; actual shortfall unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A collateral shortfall would create an equity-level cash claim outside MGM interest expense, recurring OE and the current bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We currently also provide shortfall guarantees of the $3.01 billion and $3.0 billion principal amount of indebtedness (and any interest accrued and unpaid thereon) of the landlords of Bellagio and Mandalay Bay and MGM Grand Las Vegas, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The guarantees exist, but payment depends on future landlord default, exhaustion of lender remedies and collateral value falling below the debt obligation. No present shortfall is demonstrated, and the Bellagio guarantee’s recorded fair value is described as immaterial. The $6.01 billion face amount is not an appropriate automatic deduction because MGM guarantees only the shortfall, not the full debt; nevertheless, the contingent downside should be monitored because a stressed shortfall could be material relative to the $10.672 billion base equity value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current collateral appraisals, debt balances, maturities, lender remedies, guarantee terms and associated tax consequences; calculate probability-weighted and stressed shortfalls and rerun only those supported exposures.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $827.8 million of FY2022 residual D&A; eligible portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any eligible residual D&A would be added back to historical OE, increasing OE and potentially affecting trend selection rather than the current latest-actual anchor directly.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2022 $827.8m (23.8% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied quantified residual relates to FY2022, while the valuation anchors directly to FY2025 OE of $500.7 million because the record was judged too unstable for a trend. Consequently, reclassifying FY2022 D&A has zero direct effect on the selected anchor or current scenario values. It could only matter if evidence also establishes eligible residual D&A in FY2025 or causes the anchor method to change; neither is shown here.
audit_findings.action: Classify the FY2022 residual for audit completeness, but do not rerun the current valuation unless filed evidence identifies eligible residual D&A in FY2025 or a consistently corrected series supports replacing the latest-actual anchor.
